newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen says kidnappers not harming German hostages.
newsitem.headline: Yemen says kidnappers not harming German hostages.

text.p: Four German tourists kidnapped by mountain tribesmen in Yemen's rugged interior are fit and being well-treated by their captors, an official source said on Monday.
"They are in good health and are enjoying good hospitality from their kidnappers," the source told Reuters.

The hostages -- two men and two women -- were abducted on Thursday while returning to the capital Sanaa from the eastern Marib governorate. The kidnappings came less than a month after tribesmen released seven German motorcycle tourists after more than week in captivity in the southeastern Hadramaut province.
The official source said Yemeni security forces were maintaining a cordon around the kidnappers and negotiations were continuing.
"There are no worries about the tourists. Pressure is still continuing on the kidnappers and the military siege is still on," the source said.
"Negotiations are being held in order to win their release only, without the authorities making any concessions," he said. "We will not yield to any demands."
No demands by the kidnappers have been made public.

In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The demands have rarely been political and tended to involve land or water disputes.
The hostages have all been released unharmed.
The German foreign ministry said crisis centres had been set up in Bonn and at the German embassy in Sanaa to deal with the latest kidnapping.

Marib has been the site of previous hostage takings. A U.S. engineer kidnapped by Yemeni tribemen in Marib was released in February after 16 days in captivity. A French diplomat was also kidnapped in Marib in October and set free two weeks later.
